title: Quadrille dances with John Tonkin's band in Alexandria
summary: He recalls playing quadrille music at a dance near Natchitoches with John Tonkin's band, stayed seven years, and was drummer when Tonkin died.

story.theme_name: Playing for dancers: dance bands and the dances themselves
story.community_name: Dancing to the band: quadrilles, waltzes and dance sets

blocks.x: Remember any other type of dances? Did they use any quadrilles in your time or is that before? Shottishes and waltzes and any other type of music? Could you even remember the type of dancing that they used?

Well, I'll tell you what happened uh, sometime uh, later than what I'm speaking of now. I was a drummer in John Tonkin Band in Alexander, Louisiana. And we used to go play at a place, I would say about three miles from Natchitoches, you call down on Cain River. And after intermission of the dance, each night we would play out there. We had to play a quadrille dance. Play a quadrille music that is for the older people to do that particular dance. And we used to play bye bye Blackbird. But we played in a swing or in a tempo that the old people can do that regular quadrille dance. In other words, it was a jumpy swing. It wasn't too fast, but it was jumpy and you had to chop all the notes. So it would correspond with the particular dance they was doing. Because I noticed in that it was Holland Chainz partners and all like that. You had one man who stand way off

her side and call the figures. I saw on the boat they had some of the uh, same dancers. I forget the lady that the Madame Senegal or something. Name like I, she had a creole festival a few years ago. Five or six, oh maybe seven or eight years ago. On the boat you said? They had them on the boat once when Lizzie Miles and Paul Barberin played about four years ago. They had a television program once when

uh, yeah. Well I remember that. I remember that. But this particular lady, I don't think I know her. But I remember when uh, they had a little festival out on the boat. So you did get in on the quadrille dance and dance? I did. I did. Well, well, I stayed with John
Duncan, man seven years. How's that name spelled? Tunk? Tunkin. Tunkin. T-U-N-K-I-N-G.

He's originally from Alexander Louisiana. He was a band leader at 50 years. Oh really? I've heard the name but I don't remember for sure. Well, I was his drunk player when he died. After he died, we played his funeral, funeral, buried him. Then I came back to New Orleans.
